newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-JOHNSON MAKES LANCASHIRE PAY FOR MISSED CHANCES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JOHNSON MAKES LANCASHIRE PAY FOR MISSED CHANCES.

text.p: Lancashire were made to pay a heavy price for dropped catches as South African all-rounder Neil Johnson hammered a brilliant century to steer Leicestershire to 380 for five in their county championship match at Grace Road on Friday.

Johnson, who joined the county champions at the start of the season as the overseas replacement for West Indian Phil Simmons, finished with an unbeaten 134 which came off 220 balls and contained 15 fours and three sixes.
He and wicketkeeper Paul Nixon, who was unbeaten on 68, put on 165 for the sixth wicket as the Lancashire attacked toiled in vain on an easy-paced pitch.
But they put down three key catches during the day, including Johnson who was dropped at long-off when he had made 20.

Vince Wells was put down at short extra cover when he was on 60 and went on to make 95 while Aftab Habib was dropped in the slips before he had scored and then hit 38 off 35 balls with seven fours and a six.
Johnson, who took two wickets in the Lancashire innings of 373, was in blistering form reaching his 100 with a six over midwicket.
England's one-day international all-rounder Mark Ealham hit a valuable century for Kent against Nottinghamshire at Trent Bridge.
Ealham was unbeaten on exactly 100 at the close of the second day with Kent 376 for eight replying impressively to the home side's 216.
David Fulton had provided the earlier spark for Kent with an electric 94 as Nottinghamshire's bowlers struggled to sustain the pressure.
England selector Graham Gooch's poor run with the bat continued at Ilford as his mind again seemed more preoccupied with the form of others than his own.
Gooch made just four out of Essex's second innings 215 for four, Stuart Law showing the Australian selectors what they are missing with a bold 76.
That was in reply to Yorkshire's 334 in which Michael Vaughan stroked a fine 161 as Yorkshire overtook Essex's first innings total of 297.
David Leatherdale, who took five wickets for 10 runs in Worcestershire's recent one-day match against the tourists, was again the outstanding bowler for his side against Somerset at New Road.
Leatherdale, primarily a batsman, took four for 34 as the visitors struggled to 256 for eight in response to Worcestershire's 303.
But Somerset paceman Andrew Caddick did his chance of an England recall no harm with a damaging five for 64 haul in front of watching England coach David Lloyd.
Former Glamorgan batsman David Hemp (138) and Trevor Penney (86 not out) led Warwickshire to an imposing first innings total of 631 for seven declared against Hampshire at Southampton.
Hampshire's response was edgy and they slipped to eight for two, but they had recovered to 172 for three at the close with Australian batsman Matthew Hayden unbeaten on 81.
